children: OTTAWA, Sept 25 (Reuters) - Canada recorded a slightly lower C$5.14 billion ($3.63 billion) budget deficit for the first four months of the 2026/27 fiscal year as government revenues grew faster than expenditures, the finance ministry said on Friday.    By comparison, the deficit in the same period a year earlier had been C$7.79 billion, it said in a statement.    Revenues over the four-month period increased by 7.4% largely reflecting higher income from personal and corporate income tax revenues. Expenses grew by 5.1%, driven by transfers for Old Age Security, increased operating costs and other transfer payments.    Public debt charges increased by 7.4%, largely reflecting higher average effective interest rates on an increased stock of marketable bonds, the ministry said.    On a monthly basis, Canada's deficit increased sharply to C$4.77 billion in July, compared to a C$1.51 billion deficit in July 2025.    ($1 = 1.4146 Canadian dollars)
(Reporting by Promit Mukherjee, editing by David Ljunggren)    ((Reuters Ottawa bureau; david.ljunggren@tr.com))
